clue.text: Leeway given as barge fell back

parts.note: to barge is to shove your way through with the arms, to elbow

indicators.note: back says the word for fell is read from right to left

parts.note: a fell is a stretch of upland moor in northern England

explanation.surface: Room for manoeuvre was allowed when a canal boat slipped backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barge' looks like a boat but is the verb to push. 'back' turns MOOR into ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway and space to move freely are synonyms: both mean room for manoeuvre.

clue.text: Duck's bill almost flat on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says the shortened word for flat wraps around the bill
almost drops the last letter of the word for flat

parts.note: flat as in level, even
a bill is a poster or advert, AD for short

explanation.surface: A duck's beak is nearly flat on its outer surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is the verb to dodge, not the bird, and 'bill' is an advertisement, not a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to dodge or avoid it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: British medic hasn't started to develop

indicators.note: hasn't started says the first letter of the word for medic is missing

parts.note: a surgeon is a kind of medic

explanation.surface: A British doctor has yet to begin training or to grow in the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to grow or flourish, as buds do in spring: a close synonym.

clue.text: Reporter's measured progress through water

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the news, so the word for measured is heard rather than read

parts.note: measured as on scales, weighed

explanation.surface: A journalist's steady advance across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk through shallow water is the core sense of the verb.

clue.text: 50 in old city having no siblings

indicators.note: in places the Roman fifty inside the other letters

parts.note: NY is New York City
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people in an ancient town have no brothers or sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: An only child is one with no brothers or sisters, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Doctor, always welcoming extra people into family celebration, …

indicators.note: welcoming means the doctor's letters take in the extra people

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine
others are additional people
AY is an old word for always, as in for aye

explanation.surface: A physician constantly lets more guests into a family party.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into the next one, a pair telling one story.
explanation.definitionFit: The day honouring mums is a family occasion, a celebration example.

clue.text: Implicit authentication partially withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the letters are taken from right to left
partially says only part of the word authentication is used

explanation.surface: A security check that was implied has been half taken back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' picks TICAT from inside authentication; 'withdrawn' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is understood without being stated, so implicit is a synonym.

clue.text: … looks away as nudists are milling around

indicators.note: milling around pictures a crowd moving aimlessly, so the letters of nudists are are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mum, on her special day, averts her eyes as naked people wander about.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with the previous clue: the celebrating mother looks away from the nudists.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert one's gaze is a phrasal verb synonym of looking away.

clue.text: Exclusive clubs start to thaw, perhaps when fellow leaves

indicators.note: start to points at the opening letter of the word clubs, which begins the answer
leaves says the fellow's letter goes out of the word for thaw

parts.note: thawing is one example of turning to liquid, liquefying
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: Members-only clubs begin to warm up once a man departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is an exclusive set, so the adjective describes a group keeping others out.

clue.text: Heroes met surprisingly small group

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests something turned out unexpectedly, so the letters of Heroes met are mixed

explanation.surface: Champions encountered an unexpectedly modest gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three is a small group, an example of the definition.

clue.text: First-rate leader resolved row about stray dog

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords

indicators.note: resolved as in broken down into parts, so leader is rearranged
about says the row word goes around the stray word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as in theatre seating
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A top boss sorted out a quarrel over a wandering hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges LEADER to REDALE; 'row' is a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Yorkshire terrier breed is an example of a dog.

clue.text: They say the writer had checked out

indicators.note: they say signals a spoken version of the writer's contraction

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I, and I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: People report that the author had left the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye someone is to look them over, so checked out is a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Cheer as soprano divides fortune tenor's lost

indicators.note: divides says the soprano letter splits the shortened fortune word
lost says the tenor's letter is missing

parts.note: a fortune is a treasure

explanation.surface: A singer cheers up as the soprano shares out a fortune the tenor has lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to comfort them and restore their confidence, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Blush like a wanton unlikely to run

parts.note: to colour is to blush
fast in the old sense of promiscuous, as a wanton is

explanation.surface: Redden like a shameless woman who would never flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' is dye bleeding in the wash, not fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric with fixed dyes will not bleed in the wash, so its dye does not run.

clue.text: Where to store papers from the Raj, one after another?

definitions.text: Where to store papers from the Raj
definitions.meaning: a folder for documents from British-ruled India, read jokingly
in single file, people walking in a line

explanation.walkthrough: The Raj was British rule in India; the phrase normally means walking in a single line.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking in single file means people follow one behind another in a line.

clue.text: Homes in on drinks trendy Italian banker's imported

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so the pieces go inside the drinks

parts.note: pints of beer are drinks
in means fashionable
the Po is an Italian river, something with banks

explanation.surface: A fashionable Italian financier smuggles in drinks and targets them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a river, a crossword joke: something with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinpoint a target is to locate it exactly, as one homes in on it.

clue.text: Whip mainly blames peer for letting things through

indicators.note: to whip is to beat up, as eggs are, so the letters are churned
mainly means most of, so the last letter of blames goes

explanation.surface: A party whip mostly holds a fellow peer responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' looks like the parliamentary officer but signals the anagram of BLAME plus PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A porous substance allows liquids or gases to pass, so letting things through describes it.

clue.text: Is mum OK?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically: someone silent utters nothing, a zero, O
an OK is permission or authority, a noun

explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' means silent, not a mother: someone keeping quiet utters a zero, O, so the first reading is a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on someone's authority means having their approval, their permission.

clue.text: Set placard in southern port

indicators.note: in puts the placard's letters inside the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port in the southern hemisphere
a placard advertises, an ad

explanation.surface: A sign has been placed in a harbour down south.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless set is a receiver, an apparatus for broadcasts.

clue.text: Detectives carry on fencing area for demo

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so carry on surrounds the area letter

parts.note: to ply a trade is to carry it on

explanation.surface: Police officers keep putting up a fence round a space for a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration shows something off, and a show is a display.

clue.text: Non-U sportsman following in car is unlikely to be caught

indicators.note: following puts the trimmed sportsman after the car

parts.note: an Audi is a make of car

indicators.note: Non-U, without U: the sportsman loses that letter

parts.note: a Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsman who has represented the university

explanation.surface: An unrefined athlete trailing in a car is hard to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper-class; here it just means minus U. 'caught' is heard, not arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that cannot be heard is one the ear fails to catch.

clue.text: Good French soldier ultimately wanting stroke of luck

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: ultimately wanting says the soldier lacks the last letter

parts.note: an Anzac is an Australian or New Zealand soldier

explanation.surface: A decent French soldier, in the end, hopes for a bit of luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall bringing sudden riches is a lucky break.

clue.text: Cherish men forgoing male hour during function

indicators.note: forgoing means giving up, so men gives up its male letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: during puts the hour inside the function

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Treasure the chaps who go without one man for an hour at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To enshrine a memory is to preserve it as precious, to cherish it.

clue.text: Bird speed

definitions.meaning: a wading shorebird of the sandpiper family
a nautical mile per hour, a unit of speed at sea

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a sandpiper-like wader and a ship's unit of speed.

clue.text: Delicious snack using last of meat for priest

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the meat's end letter replaces the priest's letter

parts.note: a pasty is a pastry snack

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of meat

explanation.surface: A tasty snack made with the end of the meat in place of the priest.
explanation.walkthrough: A pasty is a Cornish pastry pie; its P becomes T.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicious food is full of flavour, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Crack judge getting libel case dismissed

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, and dismissing them leaves the middle

explanation.surface: A judge throws out a libel suit with a wisecrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case dismissed' sounds legal but strips the outer L's off libel.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a jeering remark, a taunt, which is what a jibe is.

clue.text: Frivolous female banter

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, back-chat

explanation.surface: A light-hearted woman's teasing chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A flippant, glib remark is frivolous, not serious.

clue.text: Adult in risible scandal rocked holiday resort

indicators.note: in puts the adult letter among the shuffled letters
rocked means shaken up, so risible scandal is rearranged

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up mixed up in a laughable scandal shook a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocked' rearranges RISIBLE SCANDAL into BLEARICISLANDS, and A goes in after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca, Minorca and Ibiza form a Mediterranean group popular for holidays.

clue.text: Little man scratching my back in alien land

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters inside the alien

parts.note: ET is the film extra-terrestrial, an alien

indicators.note: back says the remaining letters are read in reverse
scratching means striking out, so my is removed

parts.note: a pygmy is a very small person

explanation.surface: A small man rubs my back in a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching' removes MY from PYGMY, leaving PYG; 'back' turns it to GYP.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is an example of a country, a land.

clue.text: Ideal place acquired by Virgin on far side of river

indicators.note: on far side of puts the Virgin piece after the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: acquired by means taken in, so the Virgin's name holds the place letters

parts.note: Mary, the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: A perfect spot bought by the Virgin across the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Exemplary conduct serves as a model, which is what ideal means.
